definitions.explanation: An established set of technical requirements or criteria that products, services, or processes must meet. Used for industrial standards, quality standards, and technical specifications.

examples.japanese: この{製品|せいひん}は{国際|こくさい}{規格|きかく}に{適合|てきごう}している。
examples.english: This product conforms to international standards.

examples.japanese: {安全|あんぜん}{規格|きかく}を{満|み}たさない{商品|しょうひん}は{販売|はんばい}できない。
examples.english: Products that don't meet safety standards cannot be sold.

examples.japanese: {各国|かっこく}で{充電器|じゅうでんき}の{規格|きかく}が{異|こと}なるため、{海外旅行|かいがいりょこう}には{変換|へんかん}アダプターが{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Since charger standards differ by country, you need a conversion adapter for overseas travel.

notes:
USAGE:
Common in business, manufacturing, and technology contexts. Japan's main standards body is JIS ({日本産業規格|にほんさんぎょうきかく}, Japanese Industrial Standards).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {規格|きかく}に{適合|てきごう}する (to conform to a standard)
- {規格|きかく}を{満|み}たす (to meet a standard)
- {国際規格|こくさいきかく} (international standard)
- {安全規格|あんぜんきかく} (safety standard)
- {規格外|きかくがい} (nonstandard, off-spec — also used figuratively for something extraordinary)

WATCH OUT:
- {企画|きかく}: plan, project — same reading but means planning or a planned project (e.g., {企画書|きかくしょ} "project proposal")
